column3: “What fills it” is rendered “all it contains,” and “in you” “against you.”
“About to go forth” is rendered “is coming forth.”
“Cleft” is rendered “split,” and “on a slope” “down a steep place.”
“Transgression” is rendered “rebellion”; “the high places of Judah” is rendered in the singular, “the high place.”
“Heap of ruins of the field” is rendered “a heap of ruins in the open country.”
“Daughters of an ostrich” is rendered “ostriches”; NASB renders the cohortatives with “must.”
NASB keeps the place names; the Hebrew wordplays (“Beth-le-aphrah” and “dust”) are not reproduced.
“Pass on” is rendered “Go on your way,” and “nakedness shame” “shameful nakedness”; “its standing ground” is rendered “its support,” and NASB adds “He will take.” The meaning is uncertain.
“She is in anguish for good” is rendered “Becomes weak waiting for good”; the meaning of the verb is uncertain.
“Steed” is rendered “team of horses,” and “transgressions” “rebellious acts.”
“To Moresheth-gath” is rendered “On behalf of Moresheth-gath,” and “a deceitful thing” “a deception.”
NASB adds “Moreover”; “will come to Adullam” is rendered “will enter Adullam.”
“Shear” is rendered “cut off your hair,” and “on the children” “Because of the children.”
